plan.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) and blood pressure: the ATTAIN-1 (obesity without diabetes) and ATTAIN-2 (type 2 diabetes) analyses showing lower systolic blood pressure vs placebo (reported Nov 8, 2026)
plan.angle: Frame it as post hoc analyses of two placebo-controlled trials, presented at AHA 2026 as a conference abstract and not yet a full peer-reviewed paper. Give the pooled 72-week figures in separate sentences, with population and size: ATTAIN-1 (3,127 adults with obesity, no diabetes), 6.1 vs 0.8 mmHg. ATTAIN-2 (1,613 adults with type 2 diabetes), 4.9 vs 1.5 mmHg. Say 'all doses combined' unless arm-level numbers are verified in the abstract. Weight line: 'Weight loss explained much of the drop, about 58% and 81%, and researchers think part of it may be independent of weight loss.' Blood pressure wasn't the trials' main goal. No comparison or ranking against tirzepatide. Keep the 'never change your blood pressure medicines on your own' line, and add 'dizziness or light-headedness is worth telling your doctor about'. Include all the required lines. Title: 'Orforglipron and Blood Pressure: 2 Trials #shorts' or similar. Use the generic name first, and don't put 'Foundayo' in the title.
plan.working_title: Orforglipron and Blood Pressure: What Trials Found #shorts
plan.why: A fresh randomized result (Nov 8) that qualifies for the 13:00 lead slot. Orforglipron is a searched name (3.81% CTR) and interest in the pill keeps growing. Our earlier blood-pressure Short got 132 views, and competition is low. | fact-check: Verified via Pharmacy Times (AHA Scientific Sessions, Nov 6–9, 2026, abstract #7876). These are POST HOC analyses. Calling them 'secondary analyses' is too soft. The 72-week results: in ATTAIN-1 (3,127 adults with obesity, no diabetes), pooled orforglipron lowered SBP by 6.1 mmHg vs 0.8 mmHg on placebo. In ATTAIN-2 (1,613 adults with type 2 diabetes, BMI 27 or higher), it was 4.9 vs 1.5 mmHg. Results are pooled across doses, not per arm, so the 'per arm' request can only be met if the abstract reports arms. Weight loss explained about 58% (ATTAIN-1) and 80.8% (ATTAIN-2) of the change, and investigators said the effect was 'at least in part independent of weight loss'. Media reports confirm the FDA approval (Foundayo, adults with obesity or overweight with weight-related conditions). April 2026 is supported. Confirm the exact Apr 1 date on Lilly's release. It's a conference abstract, not a peer-reviewed paper. Say so.

package.title: Orforglipron Lowered Blood Pressure in 2 Trials #shorts
package.description:
Quick answer: in ATTAIN-1 and ATTAIN-2 post hoc analyses, the GLP-1 pill orforglipron (all doses combined) lowered systolic blood pressure more than placebo over 72 weeks.

ATTAIN-1 (3,127 adults, obesity/overweight, no diabetes; all doses combined): -6.1 mmHg vs -0.8 on placebo. ATTAIN-2 (1,613 adults, type 2 diabetes + overweight/obesity): -4.9 mmHg vs -1.5 on placebo. Weight loss explained about 58% and 81% of the drop, but at least part appeared independent of it. Blood pressure wasn't the trials' main goal. This is a 2026 heart conference abstract, not yet published in a journal.

Never change your blood pressure medicines on your own. Tell your doctor about dizziness or light-headedness.

Sources: Pharmacy Times, ATTAIN-1/ATTAIN-2 BP analyses (2026) https://www.pharmacytimes.com/view/orforglipron-lowers-systolic-bp-in-attain-1-attain-2-analyses · ATTAIN-1, NEJM 2025 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40960239/ · ATTAIN-2, Lancet 2025 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41275875/

#orforglipron #ATTAIN1 #ATTAIN2 #GLP1 #BloodPressure

Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

New post hoc analyses of two orforglipron trials (ATTAIN-1 and ATTAIN-2), presented at a November 2026 heart conference, looked at this exact question.

factcheck.summary:
I checked every number against Pharmacy Times' report on the post hoc ATTAIN-1/ATTAIN-2 analyses presented at AHA Scientific Sessions 2026 (Nov 6–9, Chicago). All of them match:
- ATTAIN-1: 3,127 adults with obesity, no diabetes. Pooled orforglipron lowered systolic blood pressure by 6.1 mmHg vs 0.8 on placebo at 72 weeks.
- ATTAIN-2: 1,613 adults with type 2 diabetes and BMI 27 or higher. Systolic fell 4.9 vs 1.5 mmHg.
- Weight loss explained about 58% of the drop in ATTAIN-1 and 80.8% in ATTAIN-2. The script's line "at least in part independent of weight loss" is the source's own wording.

**Framing:** The hedges are right: post hoc, placebo-controlled, a conference abstract, blood pressure not the main endpoint. The 72-week timeframe, the populations and "all doses combined" (the source says "pooled") are all accurate. The "obesity or overweight" wording for ATTAIN-1 fits the trial's entry rules (BMI 30 or higher, or 27 or higher with a weight-related condition).

**Safety and ending lines:** They are spoken and shown in the right order: don't change your medicines, then "Not personal advice", then the prescriber line. The dizziness line is our own advice and correctly has no source tag. The Exp F line and the closing line are present.

**Word count:** 170 exactly, which is at the limit.

**Sources:** The two PubMed records are real and match the trials: ATTAIN-1 is in NEJM 2025 (PMID 40960239) and ATTAIN-2 is in The Lancet 2025 (PMID 41275875). Direct fetches of those PubMed pages and of the ClinicalTrials.gov registry page (NCT05869903) loaded no content, so I confirmed all three through search results instead. The fixes below are minor wording polish only.

issues.claim: Not yet published in a journal
issues.problem: AHA abstracts usually appear in a Circulation supplement, so 'not published in a journal' may be technically wrong. What the source actually says is that these are post hoc conference findings, not a published peer-reviewed paper.
issues.fix: Narration: "Not yet a peer-reviewed paper." On-screen: "Post hoc · Not yet a peer-reviewed paper". List item: "Not yet a peer-reviewed paper"

issues.claim: Orforglipron lowered blood pressure in 2 trials
issues.problem: There's no comparator on screen. Under the muted-viewer test, randomized results should say 'compared with placebo'.
issues.fix: Orforglipron lowered blood pressure vs placebo in 2 trials

issues.claim: Drop explained by weight loss: ATTAIN-1, ATTAIN-2
issues.problem: The label doesn't say which measure (systolic) or pair each percentage with its trial.
issues.fix: Share of systolic drop explained by weight loss: ATTAIN-1 ~58%, ATTAIN-2 ~81%

issues.claim: …all doses combined, the top number fell six point one millimeters of mercury.
issues.problem: The craft rule is to give each decimal its own short sentence. Here the decimal sits inside a long run-on sentence, which risks the TTS dropping 'point'.
issues.fix: Both: seventy-two weeks. Three thousand one hundred twenty-seven adults with obesity or overweight, no diabetes. All doses combined. The top number fell six point one millimeters of mercury. Placebo: zero point eight.

audio.soundNotes: Music under speech measured right at the center of target (-13.5 dB); trimmed slightly (0.85x) so pauses settle near -12.5 dB instead of the hotter -11 dB measured, without pushing under-voice below -15. Thinned out redundant simultaneous SFX pairs (swell+whoosh, swoosh+whip, pop+tick, etc.) to one sound per transition to respect the 3-4-per-second ceiling, trimmed a handful of cues that crept above -14 dB during speech (e.g. the back-to-back swooshes around 25-27s and 38-39s), and boosted the three 'ding' accents on the key numeric reveals (6.1 vs 0.8, 4.9 vs 1.5, and the 72-week label) so they land as a felt accent without crossing into competing-with-voice territory.
